transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, well, I guess what finally made me call the employee assistance program at work is that I'm... I'm just barely sleeping right now. I'll lie there in bed replaying stuff from work or arguments from home, and then I usually end up waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning. By the time I actually have to start the day, I just feel like I never really rested at all.
Can you tell me when this trouble sleeping first started, and whether it began around the same time as a particular stressful event or change in your life?
Um, it's been going on for about a year and two months now. And yeah, it definitely started right around the time the arguments at home started getting a lot worse.
Besides the situation at home, do you find yourself worrying excessively about several different things—like work, health, or finances—on most days, and do you have trouble controlling that worry?

No, not really. I mean, I stress about work sometimes, like anyone does, but it's not like I'm worrying about everything all the time. It's really just the stuff at home that keeps me up. I don't feel like I'm constantly on edge about my health or money or anything like that.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down, depressed, or noticing that you've lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah, I have. Um, it's been pretty constant lately. Most days, I just feel... down. It's like this heavy, gray mood just kind of follows me everywhere. I feel it at the office, in the car on the way home, and then when I'm at the house. Even when nothing specific is going on or going wrong, I just feel kind of hollow inside.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy—like hobbies, spending time with friends, or other activities—over this same period?

Yeah, I have. I used to really look forward to things like playing pickup basketball, bowling nights, going to music festivals, or even just firing up the smoker for friends on the weekend. But lately, I just... I don't know, I either end up canceling on everyone, or if I do actually show up, I feel like I'm just going through the motions. I'm not really getting any enjoyment out of any of it anymore.
Have you had any thoughts of death, dying, or that life isn't worth living, or any thoughts of harming yourself?

Well, um... I'm not making a plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But... I don't know, the thought does come up more than I want to admit. Just this feeling that maybe everyone would be better off if I just didn't wake up one morning. It's not that I want to do anything, it's just... it crosses my mind.
Have you also noticed a significant drop in your energy level or increased fatigue nearly every day during this same period?

No, not really. I mean, my energy levels have been pretty normal, I think. I still have the physical energy to get through the day at work and everything, I just... don't really have the desire to do much else. But no, I wouldn't say I've been feeling unusually tired or fatigued.
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating, thinking clearly, or making decisions nearly every day during this same period?

Yeah, I actually have. At work, I used to be able to knock out sales forecasts and put together client decks pretty quickly. But lately... I don't know, I'll find myself reading the same slide like five times. I just end up second-guessing every single number, and even after all that, I still can't decide what to say. It's definitely been a lot harder to focus and make decisions.

Have you ever had a period—lasting several days or more—where you felt unusually elevated, euphoric, or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual but still felt full of energy, or found yourself making impulsive decisions or taking risks you normally wouldn't?

No, I've never had anything like that. I've never felt unusually high or anything, and I definitely need my sleep. I haven't really done anything impulsive or risky either. It's just been this... low feeling, but never the opposite.

You mentioned this down, heavy mood and loss of interest have been pretty constant lately—can you tell me exactly how long you've been feeling this way, and whether there's ever been a stretch of two months or more during that time when you felt essentially back to your normal self?

It's been going on for about a year and two months now. It started around the time the arguments at home started getting a lot worse. And no, I haven't had any stretch where I felt back to normal for two months or anything like that. It's just been pretty much like this the whole time since it started.
